A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StableMaterials study. All 11 pages of each were compared, including equations, figures, tables, references and the additional examples on pages 10–11. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original material-generation experiments, inference measurements, VAE reconstruction errors in Table 1, and ablations in Figures 8–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original generation experiments, inference measurements, reconstruction results and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same VAE architecture, semi-supervised adversarial training, latent-consistency distillation, features rolling and refinement pipeline.

E1.justification: Both use MatSynth, Deschaintre et al. (2018) materials and SDXL-generated textures. Image/text prompting and in-domain/out-domain evaluation coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains MatFuse, MatGen and MaterialPalette for image prompting. Figure 7 retains MatFuse, MatGen and Substance 3D Sampler for text prompting.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the original splits, 6,198 PBR materials, 4,000 texture-text pairs, training budgets and inference procedures. The RMSE evaluation in Table 1 is unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same VAE architecture, semi-supervision, refinement and high-resolution generation ablations in Table 1 and Figures 8–10. The failure examples in Figure 11 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the fixed-seed inference description in Section 4.2. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are identical, including Figures 12–13 on the final pages. Table 1 retains basecolor RMSEs of 0.030 for Multi-E and 0.028 for Single-E; Section 4.2 retains the same timing and memory measurements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Section 3, including the supervised and adversarial objectives in Equations 1–2, are unchanged. No proofs or formal results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims. Although the title is shortened, knowledge distillation remains an explicit claimed contribution alongside semi-supervised learning and efficient tileable material generation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the comparisons and ablations are identical. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning spatial relations, complex figures and incorrect reflectance properties, together with the same suggested remedies.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures remain identical, including RTX4090 hardware, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, iteration counts and inference settings. The stated public-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the references and the substantive positioning against prior work are unchanged. The shortened title does not alter the retained novelty claims about distillation.

P1.justification: v2 removes 'Knowledge Distillation and' from the title and running headers and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13, Table 1, captions and body-page layouts are unchanged. Visual differences are confined to the title, running-header wording and version stamp covered under P1.

improvement.justification: v2 shortens the title while preserving the same scientific content, experimental evidence, limitations and reproducibility information. This limited editorial change provides no evidence of a meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
